fullText:
Summary: Ceylon Hospitals PLC (CHL.N0000), owner of Durdans Hospital in Colombo, is a steady, profitable business: revenue grew 17% to Rs 11.0bn and profit 46% in the year to March 2026, and the June 2026 quarter was up another 6%. At Rs 59.40 the voting share trades at 0.8x its NAV of Rs 71.56 and 10.3x trailing earnings. That looks cheap against NAV, but the NAV is mostly revalued hospital property and the return on equity is only about 8%. Weighing NAV, earnings and cash flow, the methods put fair value at about Rs 57.50, so the voting share is about 3% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 49 and treat under Rs 43 as a strong buy. The non-voting shares (CHL.X0000) get the same profits and dividends and cost Rs 50.00, which is about 13% below fair value; they usually trade 20–25% below the voting shares and may stay there.

Price and key figures
Price: voting Rs 59.40 and non-voting Rs 50.00 (CSE closing price, 2026-11-06). Please check them live. In April–June 2026 the voting share traded between Rs 57.60 and Rs 69.00 and the non-voting between Rs 45.00 and Rs 56.00. At 31 March 2026 they closed at Rs 60.00 and Rs 47.50. All per-share figures are after the 1-for-4 share split of March 2026.
Three months to 30 June 2026 (group, unaudited): revenue rose 9% to Rs 2.99bn and profit attributable rose 6% to Rs 288mn. EPS was Rs 1.72 against Rs 1.62. The September quarter results aren't in the folder yet (due by mid-November).
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 10.98bn (up 17%, a record), profit after tax Rs 1.05bn (up 45%), EPS Rs 5.68 (Rs 3.89), ROE 8.2%, NAV Rs 70.94. Dividends of Rs 1.00 were paid in the year, and Rs 1.10 more in June 2026.
Cash flow: operating cash flow Rs 1.67bn and capital spending Rs 0.76bn in 2025/26, leaving about Rs 0.92bn of free cash flow (about Rs 5 a share after minority interests).
Balance sheet: borrowings and overdraft about Rs 1.4bn against about Rs 2.6bn of cash, deposits and investments at June 2026, so there is net cash. Most of the Rs 14.3bn of property was revalued upward in 2023–2025.
History: EPS Rs 4.14 (2020/21), 7.25 (2021/22), 4.22 (2022/23), 2.90 (2023/24), 3.89 (2024/25), 5.68 (2025/26). ROE has been 5–13%, averaging about 8%.

Methods
NAV (Rs 71.56): 0.8x. Most of it is hospital land and buildings at valuers' prices, which earn only about 8% a year for shareholders.
Return on equity: 8.2% in 2025/26 (6.1% in 2024/25), well below a 16% cost of equity.
P/E: 10.3x trailing EPS of Rs 5.78. Year-end P/E: 10.6x (2026).
Dividends: Rs 1.10 paid in June 2026, a 1.9% yield; the payout is low (about a fifth to a third of profit).
NAV method (0.6x / 0.8x / 1.0x NAV): Rs 42.9 / 57.2 / 71.6, weighted Rs 55.8.
P/E method: Rs 44.8 / 63.0 / 81.6, weighted Rs 61.3.
Cash-flow DCF: Rs 37.0 / 56.0 / 82.1, weighted Rs 55.5.

A hospital is a steady cash business, so a cash-flow DCF suits it. Residual income and justified price to book would put it far below NAV because its ROE is so low, so I use NAV directly with a discount instead. The payout is too low for a dividend model.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 17.5% / 16% / 15%.
Free cash flow this year (Rs a share): 4.5 / 5.0 / 5.5, growing 6% / 10% / 13% at first and fading to 5% / 6% / 7% over 10 years.
EPS for the year to March 2027 × P/E: 5.6 × 8 / 6.3 × 10 / 6.8 × 12.
NAV multiple: 0.6x / 0.8x / 1.0x.
Average of the three methods: Rs 41.6 / Rs 58.7 / Rs 78.4.
Common: Sri Lankan 7–10-year government bonds yield about 12% (October 2026). Fair value is for a voting share; a non-voting share has the same claim on profits and dividends.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 57.50 (0.8x NAV), so the voting share at Rs 59.40 is about 3% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 48.90, and 25% gives Rs 43.10.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 57.50, 150 at up to Rs 48.90 and 150 at up to Rs 43.10. That averages about Rs 50.60, about Rs 25,300, against Rs 29,700 at Rs 59.40.
Realism: Rs 57.50 needs about a 3% fall in the voting share, which traded as low as Rs 57.50–57.60 in March and June 2026, so the first tier is realistic. The non-voting shares (CHL.X0000) get the same profits and dividends and cost Rs 50.00, which is about 13% below fair value; they usually trade 20–25% below the voting shares and may stay there.

Sensitivity (DCF base case, Rs per share)
Cost of equity 15%: 55.6 / 62.4 / 70.1 for first-year growth of 6% / 10% / 14%.
Cost of equity 16%: 50.0 / 56.0 / 62.7.
Cost of equity 17.5%: 43.5 / 48.5 / 54.1.

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: ROE rising above 10% as the new facilities fill up; lower interest rates; a higher dividend payout; a sale of surplus property or the business at close to NAV.
Supports a lower value: profit growth slowing after last year's jump; more competition from new private hospitals in Colombo; rising salary and drug costs; heavy spending on new buildings that earns little.

These are my estimates from the annual reports for the years to March 2024, 2025 and 2026 and the interim reports to June 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
